hints: Separate the variables so all $y$ terms are on the LHS and all $\theta$ terms are on the RHS: $\int (1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int \dfrac{1}{1 + \cos(2\theta)}\,\mathrm{d}\theta$.
Integrate the LHS using integration by parts, and integrate the RHS using the trigonometric identity $1 + \cos(2\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta$ and $\sec^2\theta$.
Substitute the initial conditions $y = 0, \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ to find the constant of integration, then set $y = 1$ and solve for $\tan\theta$.
walkthrough:
Separate the variables in the differential equation $(1 + y)(1 + \cos(2\theta))\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = \mathrm{e}^{3y}$:
$$(1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \dfrac{1}{1 + \cos(2\theta)}\,\mathrm{d}\theta$$
$$\int (1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int \dfrac{1}{1 + \cos(2\theta)}\,\mathrm{d}\theta$$

Integrate the left-hand side $\int (1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y}\,\mathrm{d}y$ by parts:
Let $u = 1 + y \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}y} = 1$.
Let $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}y} = \mathrm{e}^{-3y} \implies v = -\dfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{e}^{-3y}$.
Apply the integration by parts formula $\int u v'\,\mathrm{d}y = uv - \int u'v\,\mathrm{d}y$:
$$\int (1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y}\,\mathrm{d}y = (1 + y)\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{e}^{-3y}\right) - \int (1)\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{e}^{-3y}\right)\,\mathrm{d}y$$
$$= -\dfrac{1}{3}(1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y} + \dfrac{1}{3}\int \mathrm{e}^{-3y}\,\mathrm{d}y$$
$$= -\dfrac{1}{3}(1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y} + \dfrac{1}{3}\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{e}^{-3y}\right)$$
$$= -\dfrac{1}{3}(1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y} - \dfrac{1}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3y}$$

Integrate the right-hand side using the double-angle identity $1 + \cos(2\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta$:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{1 + \cos(2\theta)}\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \int \dfrac{1}{2\cos^2\theta}\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \sec^2\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta + C$$

Equate the integrated expressions:
$$-\dfrac{1}{3}(1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y} - \dfrac{1}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3y} = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta + C$$

Substitute the initial conditions $y = 0$ when $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ to determine the constant $C$:
$$-\dfrac{1}{3}(1 + 0)\mathrm{e}^0 - \dfrac{1}{9}\mathrm{e}^0 = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + C$$
$$-\dfrac{1}{3}(1) - \dfrac{1}{9}(1) = \dfrac{1}{2}(1) + C$$
$$-\dfrac{3}{9} - \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{1}{2} + C \implies -\dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{1}{2} + C$$
$$C = -\dfrac{4}{9} - \dfrac{1}{2} = -\dfrac{8}{18} - \dfrac{9}{18} = -\dfrac{17}{18}$$

Write the general solution with the evaluated constant:
$$-\dfrac{1}{3}(1 + y)\mathrm{e}^{-3y} - \dfrac{1}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3y} = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta - \dfrac{17}{18}$$

Substitute $y = 1$ into the equation to find $\tan\theta$:
$$-\dfrac{1}{3}(1 + 1)\mathrm{e}^{-3(1)} - \dfrac{1}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3(1)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta - \dfrac{17}{18}$$
$$-\dfrac{2}{3}\mathrm{e}^{-3} - \dfrac{1}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta - \dfrac{17}{18}$$
$$-\dfrac{6}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3} - \dfrac{1}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta - \dfrac{17}{18}$$
$$-\dfrac{7}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta - \dfrac{17}{18}$$

Isolate $\dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta$ and multiply by $2$ to solve for $\tan\theta$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\tan\theta = \dfrac{17}{18} - \dfrac{7}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3}$$
$$\tan\theta = 2\left(\dfrac{17}{18} - \dfrac{7}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3}\right)$$
$$\tan\theta = \dfrac{17}{9} - \dfrac{14}{9}\mathrm{e}^{-3}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Separable Differential Equations: Separates variables to $(1+y)e^{-3y}dy = (1/(1+\cos 2\theta))d\theta$ (B1). Integrates LHS by parts (M1). Obtains $-(1/3)(1+y)e^{-3y} + \int (1/3)e^{-3y}dy$ (A1). Obtains $-(1/3)(1+y)e^{-3y} - (1/9)e^{-3y}$ (A1). Integrates RHS using $1+\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta$ to $(1/2)\tan\theta$ (B1B1). Evaluates constant $C = -17/18$ using $(0, \pi/4)$ (M1). Substitutes $y = 1$ (DM1). Obtains exact value $\tan\theta = 17/9 - (14/9)e^{-3}$ (A1).
